question.worked_solution:
First, let's remove the negative sign from the variable. To do this, we multiply both sides of the equation by $-1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{x}{12} & =-\frac{1}{6} \\ (-1)\cdot (-\frac{x}{12}) & =(-1)\cdot (-\frac{1}{6}) \\ \frac{x}{12} & =\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

In the equation above, $x$ is being divided by $12.$ To isolate $x$, we can perform the opposite operation, which is *multiplying* by $12.$ So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $12$ and simplify.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{12} & =\frac{1}{6} \\ 12\cdot \frac{x}{12} & =12\cdot \frac{1}{6} \\ \frac{12x}{12} & =\frac{12}{6} \\ \frac{\cancel{12}x}{\cancel{12}} & =2 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$
